## My thinking this year

I've been growing cotton on this land for over 30 of my 40 years farming. At 64, my body isn't what it was, and it's just my wife and me at home now — the children work in the city. Nine mu of cotton is about what the two of us can handle, except at picking time when I have to bring in help.

Cotton prices haven't been great the last few years, but I know cotton. I tried wheat-maize for a couple seasons back when the county pushed it, but the soil here in our village is sandy and a bit salty, and cotton tolerates it better than grain does. So I stay with cotton.

This year I'm planning much like last year, with small adjustments based on what I saw in the field:

**Land prep and planting.** I plowed in November after pulling the stalks, then I'll harrow and lay plastic film mulch in mid-April. I plant around April 20-25, when the soil at 5 cm is steady above 14°C. I use Bt hybrid seed — I buy fresh seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, around 45-50 yuan per mu. Saving cotton seed isn't worth it with hybrids; the second generation gives uneven plants. I plant in double rows under film, about 3,500-4,000 plants per mu after thinning.

**Fertilizer.** With my soil and a target around 260 kg of lint per mu, I need roughly 16-18 kg of N per mu total. I put two-thirds down as base — a 15-15-15 compound at about 40 kg/mu before planting — then topdress urea at first flower, around 10 kg/mu, and a small amount again at peak boll-setting. Cotton doesn't like too much nitrogen — the plants go all leaf and you get fewer bolls. I learned that the hard way years ago when I overdid it. I also put down some potassium sulfate, maybe 8 kg K/mu equivalent, because potassium helps boll filling and fiber quality.

**Irrigation.** I have a tube well that I share with two neighbors. Pumping costs me about 30-40 yuan per mu per irrigation with the diesel and electricity. I plan three irrigations: one at squaring if it's dry (late June), one at peak flowering (late July), one at boll-filling (mid-August). If we get good rains I'll skip the first one — every irrigation I skip is money saved.

**Pests and weeds.** Bt cotton handles bollworm well, but I still spray two or three times for aphids, mites, and plant bugs (盲蝽). I also use a pre-emergence herbicide before laying the film. Total pesticide cost runs me around 100-120 yuan per mu.

**Labor.** My wife and I do all the field management ourselves — that's about 20-25 days of work each over the season. Picking is the hard part. Cotton needs three to four picks from September through October, and we can't keep up alone. I hire two or three people from the village for picking days, paying around 100 yuan per person per day. That's the biggest single labor cost I have.

**Yield.** Last year I got about 270 kg lint per mu. The year before was 240 because of a wet flowering period. This year I'm planning for 260 — that's realistic for my soil with normal weather.
